# Rōmy

> Rōmy helps small nonprofits find new major donors at a fraction of the cost of existing solutions.

Rōmy is a donor intelligence platform built for small nonprofit teams. It uses AI-powered prospect research to surface wealth indicators, giving histories, and affinity signals — then distills them into actionable donor profiles.

## Features

- Donor Discovery: AI-powered prospect research with wealth indicators, giving history, and affinity signals
- Fraction of the Cost: No enterprise contracts or per-seat licensing — donor intelligence at a price built for small nonprofits
- Ready to Act On: Every prospect comes with connection points, giving capacity, and outreach angles

## Blog

Field notes and industry perspective on major-gift fundraising, donor psychology, and prospect research: https://getromy.app/blog

- [The Address in Hobe Sound](https://getromy.app/blog/the-address-in-hobe-sound) — 2026-06-30, Field Notes. On the third Tuesday in January, in the small white shaker-style post office on Main Street in Litchfield, Connecticut, a mail bin behind the counter holds a heavy ivory envelope from a small Pennsylvania college, addressed to a seventy-one-year-old donor who is, on that Tuesday, four hundred and twelve miles south on a screened porch in Hobe Sound.
- [She Carries Eleven](https://getromy.app/blog/she-carries-eleven) — 2026-06-29, Industry. There is a fifty-eight-page board book that lands, every March, on the agenda of the quarterly board meeting at a regional children's hospital foundation in Wichita, and on page nineteen there is a horizontal bar that reads Director of Major and Planned Gifts — 120 active portfolios. The number has been one hundred and twenty since 2018.
- [The October She Turned Seventy-Three](https://getromy.app/blog/the-october-she-turned-seventy-three) — 2026-06-28, Field Notes. On a Tuesday morning in October, on a kitchen table in a shingled cottage on a tidal cove in Marblehead, a seventy-three-year-old woman named Patricia Halloran is re-reading, for the fourth day in a row, a tri-fold letter from Fidelity Investments.
- [The Reunion Year](https://getromy.app/blog/the-reunion-year) — 2026-06-27, Field Notes. On a Saturday morning in June, a sixty-eight-year-old woman is sitting on the velvet bench at the foot of her bed in West Hartford with a cream envelope from her college in one hand and a small porcelain cup of green tea in the other, and she has been deciding for forty-six minutes whether to drive up to her fiftieth reunion in May.

- [On Being Named in the Will](https://getromy.app/blog/on-being-named-in-the-will) — 2026-05-09, Field Notes. The wrongest sentence in fundraising is the planned-giving ask, because by the time the donor is on the phone the decision was made decades ago.
- [The Eleven-Year Yes](https://getromy.app/blog/the-eleven-year-yes) — 2026-05-08, Field Notes. The most important gift of your career is probably already in motion — you just won't see it for a decade.
- [The Thank-You Note Is the Whole Job](https://getromy.app/blog/the-thank-you-note-is-the-whole-job) — 2026-05-07, Field Notes. Most thank-yous in fundraising are receipts.
- [The Donor Your Wealth Screen Will Miss](https://getromy.app/blog/the-donor-your-wealth-screen-will-miss) — 2026-05-06, Field Notes. Quiet wealth is real wealth — and the woman in the cardigan is sitting in your CRM right now, waiting to be noticed.
